mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous one-week rebound in TRANSIT (-32.6 to -25.0) and WORKPLACES (-39.9 to -25.0) marks the restart of commuting and discretionary trip chains; because retail visits are largely non-commute-linked discretionary trips embedded in those chains, RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks above its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 7.6 points from t-1w to t-0w
fact:WORKPLACES rose 14.9 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain at or above their t-0w levels for two more weeks yet mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than -23.3, the commute-chain spillover claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS has climbed monotonically from 5.9 to 20.7 and now exceeds 20 percent above baseline; once outdoor activity normalises this far, household trip budgets shift toward combined outdoor-plus-errand outings, lifting nearby high-street retail. RETAIL_REC therefore rises over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds 20.0 percent above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 5.9 at t-3w to 20.7 at t-0w
regime_hint: relaxed outdoor-activity regime with warm-weather conditions
failure_condition: If PARKS stays above 20.0 for the next 14 days while the 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is below its last 28-day mean of -23.3, the outdoor-spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM jumping from -8.4 to -2.3 in one week is the fastest essential-trip recovery in the snapshot and signals that consumers are re-expanding overall trip volume rather than substituting; essential-trip recovery precedes discretionary retail recovery, so RETAIL_REC is higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean rises above -3.0 percent from baseline

failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above -3.0 for the next 14 days but RETAIL_REC falls further below -23.3 on average, the essential-trip lead indicator claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: The PARKS surge plus the simultaneous drop in RESIDENTIAL from 6.4 to 3.9 shows households substituting indoor and home-based time for outdoor leisure; this reallocation pulls discretionary spending minutes away from covered retail venues, so RETAIL_REC over the next week is lower than the last four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds 15.0 while RESIDENTIAL falls more than 2.0 points week-on-week

failure_condition: If the next 7-day RETAIL_REC mean is at or above -23.3 while the PARKS-plus-RESIDENTIAL substitution pattern persists, the outdoor-substitution drag is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week WORKPLACES jump of 14.9 points after four weeks below -24 is too large to be organic and indicates an administrative relaxation of mobility restrictions; policy relaxations of this size are followed by retail reopening within one to two weeks, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks when accompanied by rising TRANSIT.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -39.9 at t-1w to -25.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is below the last 28-day mean of -23.3 despite a WORKPLACES week-on-week rise exceeding 10 points, the policy-relaxation channel is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remains 3.9 points above baseline while PARKS is 20.7 above baseline, a home-anchored-but-outdoors pattern that reflects continued remote-work caution; because such households batch errands and avoid browsing retail venues, RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks stays below the last four-week mean unless RESIDENTIAL drops below 2.0.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has been positive in all four weeks, ranging 3.9 to 6.4
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 2.0 for 14 more days while the 14-day RETAIL_REC mean is at or above -23.3, the home-anchoring drag hypothesis is rejected.

failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not above its last 28-day mean of -23.3 while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain at or above -25.0, the co-movement recovery hypothesis fails.
